rationale: No candidate contains the child's distinctive mechanism: quoting headnote 3's consumption-change formula, making a USITC-report-based determination that broom consumption substantially changed since 1965, and replacing two quota quantities by the resulting adjusted figures. C23 is strongest because it likewise amends quantitative tariff provisions and substitutes revised quota-related text, while C19 concerns establishment of a tariff-rate quota and C01 uses similar TSUS-amendment and effective-date phrasing. Those similarities are standard tariff-proclamation machinery rather than evidence that any candidate materially supplied the child's drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Items 750.26 and 750.29 ... are modified by deleting the quantities 115,000 and 205,000 ... and substituting in lieu thereof 91,885 and 161,540
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The second article description preceding item 927.50 is amended ... Items 927.53 and 927.54 are deleted, and ... new items ... are substituted in lieu thereof
shared_material.explanation: C23 shares an amend-by-deletion-and-substitution technique for quota-related TSUS provisions, but not the child's consumption-indexed quota recalculation or its operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the tariff-rate quotas set forth in items 750.26 and 750.29 should be modified
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby establish a tariff-rate quota with respect to stainless steel flatware
shared_material.explanation: C19 involves a tariff-rate quota, but establishes and allocates a new quota under different trade-agreement machinery rather than recalculating an existing quota from changed domestic consumption.

shared_material.child_excerpt: shall be effective as to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on and after May 27, 1976
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall be effective as to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on and after May 1, 1972
shared_material.explanation: C01 contains nearly identical effective-date language, but this is routine tariff-proclamation boilerplate and cannot independently establish templating.
